image_description: A close-up macro photograph of an insect, identified as a tiger beetle, perched on a green leaf. The beetle features a distinctively elongated, narrow body with a metallic dark green/black thorax and abdomen covered in fine stippling. It has bright orange legs and long, thin black antennae. The head is equipped with large reddish compound eyes and visible mandibles.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is clearly visible, appearing broad relative to the narrow neck/pronotum connection, and features large, prominent reddish compound eyes consistent with the species.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Long sickle-shaped mandibles adapted for capturing prey.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Dark, curved mandibles are visible at the front of the head, matching the description of sickle-shaped predatory tools.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Filiform antennae extending well beyond the midbody.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The antennae are thread-like (filiform) and extend significantly backward, surpassing the midpoint of the body length.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Elongated, slender body with distinctly narrow proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body exhibits the characteristic 'cicindela' shape: very narrow waist and elongated elytra, distinct from broader beetles.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Bright metallic coloration in green, bronze, or copper tones.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The exoskeleton displays a deep metallic sheen, primarily dark green/bronze on the thorax and elytra base.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: There is a distinct white/pale transverse band near the tip of the elytra and lighter stippling patterns along the sides.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Six slender cursorial legs enabling rapid pursuit.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Three pairs of long, slender legs are visible (orange femurs/tibiae), consistent with a cursorial (running) adaptation.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Chitinous exoskeleton with segmented body (head, thorax, abdomen).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The three main tagmata are clearly defined and separated by flexible joints, showing a hard, chitinous texture.
